svg.title: One message, written out and then read aloud
svg.desc: Inside the nucleus, RNA polymerase copies one gene from DNA into pre-messenger RNA. The copy is capped, given a tail, and spliced so that only the exons remain. The finished mRNA leaves through a nuclear pore. In the cytosol a ribosome moves along it three bases at a time; each transfer RNA brings the one amino acid its anticodon matches, and the amino acids are joined into a polypeptide. -- Independently created. Drawn from the published mechanism in code, from scratch, on 2026-10-10. No published figure was traced, scanned, copied or adapted. Generated by the author's own scripts; the generator source is retained as the record of independent creation. Mechanism checked for accuracy against Campbell Biology in Focus, 3rd edition; no figure from that or any other book was consulted as a layout or copied in any part.

svg.text: SOL BIO MODULE 4 . DE BIO 101 . GENE EXPRESSION
One message, written out and then read aloud
The gene never leaves. A copy of it does, and the copy is what gets read.
